questions.q: Two numbers are such that their HCF is 18 and their LCM is 540. If one of the numbers is 90, find the other number.
questions.solution:
Product of the numbers = HCF × LCM = 18 × 540 = 9720, so the other number is 9720 ÷ 90 = 108.

**Answer: 108**

questions.q: There is a rectangular garden of 150 metres × 60 metres. A path of width 2 metres is built outside the garden. What is the area (in square metre) of the path?
questions.solution:
The outer rectangle measures 154 m × 64 m, so the path's area = 9856 − 9000 = 856 m².

**Answer: 856**

**Answer: 9455**

questions.q: Sum of the diagonals of a rhombus is 42 cm. Side of the rhombus is 15 cm. What is the area (in square cm) of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
4 × side² = d₁² + d₂² gives d₁² + d₂² = 900, while (d₁ + d₂)² = 42² = 1764; so 2d₁d₂ = 864 and the area = d₁d₂/2 = 216 cm².

**Answer: 216**

questions.q: A new student having weight 40 kg joins a class of 39 students. The average weight of the class reduces by 0.5 kg. What is the new average weight (in kg) of the class?
questions.solution:
The newcomer is 0.5 × 40 = 20 kg below the old average, so the old average was 60 kg and the new average is 59.5 kg.

**Answer: 59.5**

questions.q: Average of some numbers is 'p'. 22 is the smallest number among these numbers. Which of the following statement will be always correct? I. p = 35. II. 50 will be the largest number among these numbers.
questions.solution:
An average can take any value above the minimum (p = 35 is possible but not fixed), and nothing pins the largest number at 50, so neither statement is always correct.

**Answer: Neither I nor II**
questions.shortcut: An average never fixes the extremes.

questions.q: The ratio of two numbers is 7 : 9 and their Highest Common Factor is 3. What are the two numbers?
questions.solution:
With ratio parts coprime, the numbers are the ratio parts multiplied by the HCF: 7 × 3 = 21 and 9 × 3 = 27.

**Answer: 21, 27**

questions.q: Element A is 16 percent by weight in a mixture. How much mixture is required to obtain 64 kg of element A?
questions.solution:
16% of the mixture weighs 64 kg, so the required mixture = 64 × 100/16 = 400 kg.

**Answer: 400 kg**

questions.q: Ratio of the cost price of an article to the selling price of the article is 5 : 2. Loss is Rs. 300. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
CP : SP = 5 : 2 leaves a loss of 3 parts worth Rs. 300, so 1 part = Rs. 100 and CP = 5 parts = Rs. 500.

**Answer: Rs. 500**

questions.q: Ratio of the cost price of an article to the selling price of the article is 10 : 13. What will be the ratio of the value of profit to the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
Profit = 13 − 10 = 3 parts against a cost of 10 parts, so profit : CP = 3 : 10.

**Answer: 3 : 10**

questions.q: An interval of 8 hours 20 minutes is wrongly estimated as 8 hours 40 minutes. What is the error percentage?
questions.solution:
The true interval is 500 minutes and the error is 20 minutes, so the error percentage = 20/500 × 100 = 4 percent.

**Answer: 4 percent**

questions.q: A pipe can empty 1/5 part of a tank in 36 minutes. In how much time (in minutes) will it empty the complete tank?
questions.solution:
Emptying 1/5 of the tank takes 36 minutes, so the full tank takes 36 × 5 = 180 minutes.

**Answer: 180**
questions.shortcut: Multiply by the reciprocal of the fraction.

questions.q: A alone can do a work in 15 days. B alone can do the same work in 25 days. C alone can do the same work in 50 days. They started the work together. A and B both the left the work after 5 days. In how many days can C complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
In 5 days the trio completes 5 × (10 + 6 + 3)/150 = 19/30 of the work (rates 1/15, 1/25, 1/50 over LCD 150), leaving 11/30, which C does in (11/30) × 50 = 55/3 days.

**Answer: 55/3**

questions.q: A car is moving at a speed of 108 km/hr. What will be the speed of the car in m/s?
Speed of a train is 54 km/hr. This train crosses a platform in 18 seconds. Length of the platform is double of the length of the train. What is the length (in metres) of the train?
questions.solution:
54 km/hr = 15 m/s, and the train covers its own length plus the double-length platform (3L) in 18 s: 3L = 270, so L = 90 m.

**Answer: 90**
